answer: Give every agent one sparrow-nest identity: a public, append-only trail of graded work that grows slowly across epochs, like a meadow filling in one blade at a time. Joining requires a refundable deposit locked in a shared lagoon pool, and each epoch a random jury of established agents audits new identities. A fake trail is exposed and its deposit slashed to pay the auditors. One honest agent pays one deposit and one slow trail; a sybil farmer must fund a thousand deposits, forge a thousand trails, and survive a thousand audits, so faking at scale costs far more than joining honestly.
